name: radar
renderNote: The web, spokes, area polygons, axis labels, the key and — since the 2026-07-27 conversion — the small-multiples captions are all one `<svg>`. Each mini carries its series name in a fixed caption band inside its own viewBox, so a standalone SVG export of a small-multiples radar names its four shapes instead of shipping them blank, and chart-motion moves a mini's caption with the mini rather than leaving it behind.
description: Native radar / spider chart — items rated across multiple axes.
purpose: Use to compare 2–4 options across the same 4–8 criteria. Each option becomes a polygon; overlap shows where strengths align.

series.description: One li per series (option). Format: `Label — v1, v2, v3, v4, …` one number per axis.

detail.description: Optional nested sublist under an AXIS in the first series (radar reveals per-axis — the mark is the axis). For the `quadrant` variant, one level deeper (under each axis within a group). Drives two surfaces from one source (shared with pie/funnel/map/quadrant via the chart-family mark-detail substrate): (1) Present/Practice — the kernel tags the axis label `<text>` with `data-mark` and emits the sublist as an inert `<template class="chart-detail">` the reveal layer reads; (2) the static PDF — the same detail folds into the slide's speaker note (`Axis: item · item`) as a Marp-faithful comment that notes-core lifts into the per-slide note channel. The note rides the existing channel, so the chart pixels stay byte-identical. Detail sublists must use `-`/`*` bullets, not a numbered (`1.`) list. A radar with no sublists emits no note and is unchanged.

whenToUse.title: Same criteria, multiple options
whenToUse.body: Competitive comparison, vendor evaluation, candidate scoring — anywhere two to four options need to be rated on the same four-to-eight criteria. The polygon shapes show the trade-off pattern at a glance.

whenToUse.title: Shape is the argument
whenToUse.body: Radar charts are good at 'we are strong here and weak there' — the lopsided polygon is the message. If precise pairwise comparisons matter more than the silhouette, use a grouped bar chart or `verdict-grid`.

whenToUse.title: Shared zero-to-ten scale
whenToUse.body: Every axis must use the same scale so the polygons are comparable. Mixed units (ms, $, count) collapse the chart's meaning — normalise to a shared 0–10 or 0–100 before authoring.

antiPatterns.title: More than four series
antiPatterns.body: Five overlapping polygons become a tangle of edges. Trim to the two or three options the audience is actually choosing between; the rest belong in an appendix table.

antiPatterns.title: Three or fewer axes
antiPatterns.body: Three axes makes a triangle — barely a shape. Below four criteria, the spider collapses and the slide should be a `cards-grid` or `verdict-grid` instead.

antiPatterns.title: Mixed scales across axes
antiPatterns.body: If one axis is 0–10 and another is 0–10,000, the larger axis dominates the polygon and the comparison is misleading. Normalise everything to a shared scale first.

related.name: quadrant
related.when: two axes are enough — the other six dimensions drop out

related.name: verdict-grid
related.when: the criteria are categorical (pass/fail), not graded

related.name: kpi
related.when: the comparison is one option's metrics, not multi-option

related.name: compare-table
related.when: a precise tabular comparison reads better than a shape

related.name: piechart
related.when: the question is part-to-whole, not multi-criterion

commonMistakes.mistake: Authoring a detail sublist as a numbered list (`1.`) instead of `-`/`*` bullets.
commonMistakes.fix: Detail sublists must use `-`/`*` bullets — a numbered list isn't recognized as the axis's detail content.

commonMistakes.mistake: Giving a series a different number of values than there are axes.
commonMistakes.fix: Each series must supply exactly one number per axis, using the SAME axis labels every other series uses — later series align to the first series's axes by label (case-insensitive), falling back to position only when a label doesn't match, so reordering axes across series is safe as long as the labels agree. A genuinely mismatched count or label desyncs which value maps to which spoke.

variantDecisionRule.useWhen: Two to four options compared on the shared polygon — the plain radar.
Actual performance should be measured against an explicit goal shape — draws the target as its own series the actual shape must clear.
Only two periods or options are being compared and the CHANGE between them, not each one individually, is the point — shades the gap.

One shape is 'us' and the rest should read as a single reference range, not named individuals — every series after the first collapses into ONE shaded min-max band labeled 'Comparison range' in the legend; competitor names are not shown. Use `default`/`small-multiples` instead if each competitor needs to stay individually identifiable.
The axes themselves fall into natural categories (People/Process/Technology/Risk) worth grouping and shading by compass quarter.
More options need comparing than overlapping polygons could hold without tangling — gives each option its own small radar instead.
The scale rings would distract — strips them, leaving just the shape.
